docs.title: Plugmix for FontLab
docs.text:
Use the Extensions pack with App's fontlabapp.plugins core: 50 plugins: 39 reporters, five Filters, four Tools, one Palette and one General plugin. The retained fontlab_plugmix compatibility package is a separate runtime.

The App Extensions catalogue lists all 39 reporter bundles and their limits, the eleven other bundles and the optional Show Reporters action. App discovers the Extensions at startup; enable reporters in the Reporters palette or View > Reporters. The compatibility package retains all 19 reporters and the other plugin kinds. Read installation before choosing a runtime, and development and limits before relying on native behavior. LICENSE and NOTICE retain the Apache and MIT terms.

Choose one runtime per FontLab session. Both use fontlab-plugmix.json; their startup installers and saved preferences are not interchangeable. Native cross-runtime migration and recovery remain unqualified.

This complete local source/generated website does not publish private Pages. Its configured URL is the future repository identity only. Builds import neither plugin runtime and do not start or drive FontLab.

docs.title: App Extensions catalogue
docs.text:
All 39 reporter bundles below live in Extensions/reporters/. Each has its own plugin.json and Python source; no package install or individual launcher is needed for a bundle. Bundles and the action require fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 and its providers; their API imports use fly.ap, preserving canonical App identity. App's fontlabapp.plugins core owns discovery, painter registration, preferences, rollback and teardown. fontlabapp.plugmix remains a deprecated import shim, separate from the retained fontlab_plugmix runtime.

App's startup hook discovers the Extensions folder. Enable or disable reporters in the Reporters palette or View > Reporters; enabling persists the stable ID. Reporters do not edit font geometry. Scripts/Plugmix/Show Reporters.py is the remaining optional action script: it opens the palette. Do not combine the two runtimes' startup paths. See installation for setup.

Bundle name / reporter Overlay and limits AllAngles.fontlabReporter — All Angles Angle of each straight segment from vertical, mod 180°; components excluded AnchorCloud.fontlabReporter — Anchor Cloud Names and positions of the current glyph's anchors (local anchors only) AngledHandles.fontlabReporter — Angled Handles Rings on handles off the horizontal, vertical and italic axes Blindfold.fontlabReporter — Blindfold Opaque blocks hide the strip from 70 units under the descender up to the baseline, and everything from x-height up to 70 units over the ascender (band = "cap_height" for cap height); the band between baseline and that height stays visible CenterLines.fontlabReporter — Center Lines Advance/2, x-height/2 and cap-height/2 lines ColorToner.fontlabReporter — Color Toner Each component filled in translucent black (darken = 0.15, wrapped into 0..1) so composed parts stand out from drawn outlines Crosshair.fontlabReporter — Crosshair Long guides through selected nodes; no mouse tracking DuplicateAnchors.fontlabReporter — Duplicate Anchor Rings Red/yellow rings for every anchor pair less than one unit apart OnlySelectedHandles.fontlabReporter — Emphasise Selected Handles Accent lines and rings for handles next to selected nodes GlyphFocus.fontlabReporter — Glyph Focus Shade outside the advance box between descender and ascender ImpreciseItalicAngle.fontlabReporter — Imprecise Italic Angle Straight segments within 2° of the slant but not on it KernIndicator.fontlabReporter — Kern Indicator Displayed kerning of the pairs touching the glyph, above each junction (orange positive, blue negative); shown only between 3% and 90% zoom NodeCount.fontlabReporter — Node Count Total on- and off-curve nodes; components excluded NodeIndexes.fontlabReporter — Node Indexes Contour index beside every node NodesCloseToZones.fontlabReporter — Nodes Close to Zones Rings on on-curves near zone edges or metric heights OffcurveOutsideBounds.fontlabReporter — Off-curve Handles Outside Bounds Handles beyond the on-curve bounding rectangle RSBLine.fontlabReporter — RSB Line Advance boundary with RSB and LSB labels Rekha.fontlabReporter — Rekha Viewer Head-line bar for Devanagari, Bengali and Gurmukhi letters, moved by rekha and rekha_stop anchors; suffixed or interrupted anchors are not supported SegmentLength.fontlabReporter — Segment Length Straight and flattened curve lengths SelectedCoordinates.fontlabReporter — Selected Node Coordinates Coordinates beside selected nodes ShowBackground.fontlabReporter — Show Background Outlines of the glyph's background layer filled in pale blue (alpha 0.3), counters open; background components are not shown ShowCharacter.fontlabReporter — Show Character The glyph's first Unicode as 100 px text above the glyph; hidden below 20% zoom; no base-name lookup ExportStatus.fontlabReporter — Show Export Status Red cross over the body of a glyph that is set not to export GlobalGlyph.fontlabReporter — Show Global Glyph Contours of a helper glyph named _global behind every other glyph: closed paths orange outline with faint fill, open paths blue outline with faint fill; its components are not shown and it is not drawn on itself GlyphsInLabelColor.fontlabReporter — Show Glyphs In Label Color Glyph and component outlines filled in the mark colour, counters open ShowInterpolation.fontlabReporter — Show Interpolation For each other compatible master, the glyph blended halfway (factor = 0.5) node by node between the shown layer and that master, filled in dark magenta (alpha 0.25), counters open; components are not drawn (neither the shown layer's nor the masters'); no instances, anchors or recentering, and masters with the same coordinates are skipped KerningGroupReference.fontlabReporter — Show Kerning Group Reference Members of the glyph's left kerning class drawn on top of each other as small (0.2) teal silhouettes 150 units left of the glyph, and of its right class 150 units right of it, baseline at half x-height; opacity is 0.8 divided by the class size (floor 0.04), so crowded classes read denser. Left-to-right text only. Very large classes are truncated: at most 32 glyphs are requested, alternating left and right LabelColor.fontlabReporter — Show Label Color Bar in the glyph's mark colour under the descender (placement baseline or body), slanted by the italic angle; layer marks are not distinguished ShowRotated.fontlabReporter — Show Rotated Outline turned 180° about its bounds centre; components excluded Siblings.fontlabReporter — Show Siblings Look-alike Latin letters (c/e/o, b/p, d/q/u, h/l/n/r/a) filled in green behind the glyph, fainter in larger groups; Latin groups only ShowStems.fontlabReporter — Show Stems Rings and span widths along a scan line at half x-height; components excluded SmartPlumblines.fontlabReporter — Smart Plumblines Centre lines through each contour's and the selection's extents; components excluded SmoothNodeAngles.fontlabReporter — Smooth Node Angles Handle-angle mismatch and length ratio at smooth nodes SpeedPunk.fontlabReporter — Speed Punk Colour-ramped curvature comb; components excluded StemThickness.fontlabReporter — Stem Thickness Wherever the mouse is (no proximity limit), a line across the outline from the outline point nearest it, perpendicular to it, to the nearer crossing more than 1 unit away, labelled with its rounded length; nothing at a corner where the ray runs along the outline; own contours only, no guide command or modifier key TopsAndBottoms.fontlabReporter — Tops and Bottoms Rings and y labels at the highest and lowest on-curves TwoPointDistance.fontlabReporter — Two Point Distance Segment, length and angle for exactly two selected nodes Unitizer.fontlabReporter — Unitizer Vertical grid at UPM / 18 VerticalMetrics.fontlabReporter — Vertical Metrics Labelled ascender, descender, x-height, cap-height and baseline

docs.title: Other Extensions
docs.text: The same pack supplies Extensions/filters/DeleteSmallPaths.fontlabFilter, Extensions/general/ZoomToSelection.fontlabGeneral, Extensions/palettes/StepAndRepeat.fontlabPalette and Extensions/tools/SmartSelect.fontlabTool, each with a plugin.json manifest. These provide Delete Small Paths, Zoom to Selection, Step and Repeat and Smart Select respectively. App owns their host operations; filters and palettes use its guarded writer APIs. Native Undo/Redo and saved/reopened behavior remain unverified for this installed tuple.

docs.title: New filters and tools
docs.text:
• Round Outline to Grid snaps own outline nodes to a grid.
  • Move Outlines translates outlines without changing advance widths.
  • Scale Outlines scales outlines about a chosen pivot.
  • Slant Outlines applies geometric shear.
  • Measurement Ruler measures a dragged span.
  • Node Probe inspects nearby outline nodes.
  • Contour Picker selects a contour by a nearby node.

The four coordinate filters preserve components, anchors, advance widths and native curve types. Tools do not change geometry. Their pages describe scope, parameters and interaction limits; native verification remains open.

docs.title: Painting and acceptance limits
docs.text: Center Lines, Vertical Metrics, Crosshair, Tops and Bottoms, RSB Line, Unitizer, Node Count, Smart Plumblines, Show Stems, Speed Punk, Show Rotated, Show Label Color, Show Glyphs In Label Color, Show Character, Rekha Viewer, Show Background, Color Toner, Show Global Glyph, Show Siblings, Show Kerning Group Reference and Show Interpolation draw under the native glyph layer when native canvas painters are available; the rest draw over it, and on older builds all draw over the canvas. The original seven reporters, native canvas drawing and all 18 pre-revision reporters were checked in FontLab 9; Glyph Focus and the revised slant and unit grid have offline coverage only. Node Count, All Angles, Smart Plumblines, Show Stems, Speed Punk, Show Rotated, Blindfold, Show Label Color, Show Glyphs In Label Color, Show Character, Rekha Viewer, Show Export Status, Show Background, Color Toner, Show Global Glyph, Show Siblings, Show Kerning Group Reference, Kern Indicator, Show Interpolation and Stem Thickness have offline test coverage only.

docs.title: App reporter contract
docs.text:
Write a reporter by subclassing fly.ap.plugins.Reporter with a unique name, a title and a pure compute(snapshot) that returns Mark objects (ring, line, polyline, polygon, text) in glyph units; pixel sizes are view pixels. Set layer = "background" to paint under the glyph layer. An error raised by compute or requested_glyphs goes to the error sink once per reporter and message until Plugmix is uninstalled. Every snapshot also carries identity (name, Unicodes, raw mark, mark RGB, export flag) and view.px_per_unit; either is None when it cannot be read, and the read error goes to the plugin error sink once. Mark RGB uses HSL lightness 0.65, so it differs slightly from FontLab's flag swatches (inferred, unverified natively). Offline coverage only. Opt-in class flags add costlier data: needs_components gives components (base name, transform and decomposed base contours, nested up to 8 levels), needs_background gives background (the mask's contours, () when empty, None when there is none), and needs_masters gives masters (each master's contours, anchors, advance and a compatible flag that compares contour count, node count per contour and on/off-curve pattern with the shown layer, ignoring components and open/closed state). Components and masters are cached per glyph revision and shared by all reporters; components also re-check their base glyphs. Master outlines may lag until the foreground glyph's lastModified moves, which is unverified natively. The background is read on every paint. An empty component layer means the master that owns the shown layer. Metrics also come from that master. Zones and the italic angle need a master switch to read, so when the shown layer belongs to another master the zones are empty and the italic slant is the current master's. Skipped components and failed reads go to the error sink once. Offline coverage only. needs_kerning gives kerning_groups (the classes used when the glyph is a pair's first member, left, and second member, right, with their members), read on every paint because a class edit may not move the glyph's timestamp. Override requested_glyphs(identity, kerning_groups=None) to name up to 32 other glyphs; others maps each one that exists to its own unselected contours (components skipped), cached per requested glyph's revision. Both use the master that owns the shown layer. needs_neighbours gives view.neighbours: the previous and next glyph on the same line as (name, kerning), kerning in font units as displayed (0 when kerning processing is off). Which glyph stores a pair's kerning is inferred, unverified natively. Neighbours need the native canvas painter backend; with EditorPainters, or when the view scale is unusable, they are None. Offline coverage only. needs_mouse gives view.mouse, the cursor in the glyph's own units (canvas.mousePosition() mapped back through the glyph and text-block transforms), or None when the map is not invertible. While any enabled reporter asks for it, one event filter watches the active glyph window and flushes (updateScreenRect plus updateViewport) at most once per 16 ms after mouse moves, ending with a flush after the last move. The filter goes when the last such reporter is disabled, when the active canvas changes or closes, and on uninstall(). Only the watched canvas gets a mouse; with EditorPainters it is None. Whether moves reach the filter under every tool is unverified natively. Offline coverage only. Bundles declare id, name, kind, version, entry and min_app_version in plugin.json. The ID, display name and kind must match the entry class; IDs are unique across kinds and the entry module must be inside the bundle. Invalid manifests and imports are logged and skipped. Discovery is sorted and retains class identity on repeated scans; restart FontLab to load changed source. Third-party packages can still use the retained fontlabapp.plugmix entry-point group.

Historical App native observations do not qualify activation or rendering of the current Extensions pack. Native palette/menu synchronization, toolbar placement, startup, teardown, drawing and writer history still require qualification on the exact installed App/Plugmix tuple. Issue 211 native probes remain separate.

docs.title: Compatibility package
docs.text:
src/fontlab_plugmix/ remains a separate installable package with 19 reporters, an undoable Filter, a dockable Palette, a native Tool and a General menu command. Its code, tests, dependencies and legal attribution are retained.

For this runtime, install the package and fontlab-fontlabapp in FontLab's Python 3.11 environment and explicitly call fontlab_plugmix.install() once per session. The optional initScript-snippet.py now targets App through fly.ap.plugins.install() and must not be combined with the compatibility installer. Use native MeVisLab PythonQt inside FontLab, without another Qt binding. Native per-canvas painters are preferred, with App's EditorPainters fallback on older builds.

The compatibility View menu has 19 Plugmix: Show … actions and Zoom to Selection. Glyph has Delete Small Paths; Window has Step and Repeat Panel and Tool Smart Select. Choices live in FontLab's Data directory as fontlab-plugmix.json. install(config_dir=...) selects an owned directory for tests, and boot.uninstall() removes owned actions, overlays and panels while retaining saved choices. Unknown preference keys survive. The compatibility runtime maps old nodes_outside_paths choices to offcurve_outside_bounds; this is not a cross-runtime migration guarantee.

Filter, Tool and General choices default on until explicitly changed. Palettes start hidden. Saved preferences retain enabled, enabled_filters, enabled_palettes, enabled_tools, enabled_general and last-used params.

docs.title: Compatibility reporters
docs.text:
Reporter Overlay Duplicate Anchor Rings Red/yellow rings for every unordered anchor pair less than one font unit apart; three coincident anchors produce three ring pairs. Node Indexes Full contour index beside every on- and off-curve node. Selected Node Coordinates Coordinates beside selected nodes. Two Point Distance A segment, length and angle for exactly two selected nodes. Off-curve Handles Outside Bounds Off-curve handles beyond the on-curve bounding rectangle. This uses bounds, unlike mekkablue's ShowNodesOutsidePaths path-containment test. Center Lines Advance/2, x-height/2 and cap-height/2 lines. Vertical Metrics Labelled ascender, descender, x-height, cap-height and baseline lines. Angled Handles Rings on off-curve handles outside horizontal, vertical and italic axes. Crosshair Thin, far-reaching guides through selected nodes; no mouse tracking. Tops and Bottoms Rings and y labels at tied highest and lowest on-curve positions. Segment Length Straight and flattened curve lengths where both on-curve ends are selected, or all when nothing is selected; runs of more than two off-curves are skipped. Glyph Focus Translucent shade outside the advance box between descender and ascender. Emphasise Selected Handles Accent lines and rings for handles next to selected nodes; native handles remain visible. Anchor Cloud Names and positions of the current glyph's anchors. RSB Line Advance boundary plus RSB and LSB labels from the native ink box. Unitizer Vertical grid behind the glyph at UPM / 18 increments; units per em is a class attribute. Nodes Close to Zones Rings on on-curves near selected-master zone edges or metric heights. Imprecise Italic Angle Straight segments within 2° of the master slant but not exactly on it. Smooth Node Angles Handle-angle mismatch and handle-length ratio at smooth nodes.

Anchor Cloud shows local anchors only. A font-wide cloud still needs reliable revision-based invalidation. Stroke, text and ring sizes stay constant while zooming. Center Lines, Vertical Metrics, Crosshair, Tops and Bottoms, RSB Line and Unitizer request background painting; older builds substitute foreground painting and log that choice once. Each reporter captures the glyph separately on repaint; zones and native ink bounds are read only when requested.

Native drawing maps glyph points through the glyph text-block transform, the block placement and canvas.mapToViewportF. Text-block placement matters away from the canvas origin. Native compatibility observations are historical; shortcut and keyboard cursor mapping changes still need an in-app recheck.

docs.title: Other compatibility plugins
docs.text:
• Delete Small Paths deletes closed contours below the threshold (default 400 font units squared) using flattened path area or flattened bounds area. Open contours and exact-threshold values stay. It edits selected current-master glyphs through one geometry Undo step, skips automatic layers and unsafe shared/transformed outlines per glyph, and retains safe glyphs in the selection.
  • Step and Repeat duplicates selected contours with count additional copies and repeated X/Y offsets through one geometry Undo step. It retains unselected contours, leaves copies unselected and refuses shared/transformed outlines, non-master display layers, stale contour counts and zero-offset repeats. Count zero or no selection is a no-op. Dock ownership survives temporary hiding; the Window toggle provides explicit close if close detection is absent.
  • Smart Select selects whole contours touched by a dragged rectangle; Shift toggles them. It changes selection only and omits the source plugin's double-click containment and native move handling.
  • Zoom to Selection fits the selected nodes with a margin. It omits delayed viewport adjustment and a shortcut. General font events use stable fgId identities and share the palette host's refresh timer.

docs.title: Reporter contracts
docs.text:
compute() receives immutable Python data and returns marks in font units. Native reads and writes belong in the host layer. Pure imports do not need FontLab. Current App examples import Mark and Reporter from fly.ap.plugins (Fly >=1.3.0); those are App's exact classes, not the distinct fontlab_plugmix.Reporter base.

Reporter.compute(snapshot) receives immutable data and returns Mark objects. Keep this callback pure; no implementation bodies are rendered on this site.

Publish classes derived from fontlab_plugmix.Reporter through fontlab_plugmix.plugins entry points. App classes imported through Fly use the separate fontlabapp.plugmix entry-point group alongside Extensions discovery in fontlabapp.plugins. Names must be unique and titles human-readable. Marks support ring, line, polyline, polygon and text; polygon fill is RGBA, coordinates are font units, and stroke/text/diameter values are view pixels. layer = "background" requests painting beneath native glyphs on supported builds. Callbacks contain failures; reporter compute/paint must not write font data.

docs.title: Consumer audit
docs.text: This page records who uses the compatibility package, its entry-point groups and the deprecated shim, as found in the maintained repositories on origin/main (2026-11-11). It is evidence for a removal decision, not the decision. Generated docs/, CHANGELOG, WORK, PLAN, TODO and lock-file noise are excluded. Import forms inside this package were counted per file, not classified one by one.

docs.title: Inside this package
docs.text: The bundled Extensions already import the canonical fontlabapp.plugins (50 tracked Python files: 5 filters, 1 general, 1 palette, 39 reporters, 4 tools; counted with git grep -l "fontlabapp.plugins" -- 'Extensions/*.py' and grouped by directory), as do Scripts/Plugmix/Show Reporters.py and 17 tests. The legacy src/fontlab_plugmix tree (51 tracked Python files, counted with git ls-files 'src/fontlab_plugmix/*.py') keeps its own parallel modules and the old entry-point group; 11 tests import it. No file here imports the deprecated shim.

docs.title: Lock-file membership
docs.text: No maintained lock file pins fontlab-python-plugmix. Fontport and Glyport pin fontlab-fontlabapp as an editable sibling. Seven repositories have no lock file; six others lock neither package.

docs.title: Not knowable from the workspace
docs.text:
• Third-party packages that publish either entry-point group (fontlabapp.plugmix, fontlab_plugmix.plugins).
  • Installed copies that still call the old startup snippet.

docs.title: Removal gates stay open
docs.text: Removing the compatibility package or the fontlabapp.plugmix shim stays blocked until an outside-consumer search or a deprecation period covers the two items above.

docs.title: Development and limits
docs.text:
Use arm64 Python 3.11 and owned sibling App, Pens and Fly (>=1.3.0) sources. The runner explicitly prepares Pens and selects Fly's src on PYTHONPATH. Set PLUGMIX_PENS_SOURCE or PLUGMIX_FLY_SOURCE to select other owned checkouts; the isolated-child regression selects that exact source and verifies its origin without assuming Fly is installed. The exact full recipe is:

UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system PLUGMIX_FONTLABAPP_SOURCE="$PWD/../fontlab-fontlabapp" sh test.sh

The runner-layout test requires the sibling App source directory. The no-selector run executes the complete suite and the compatibility package's coverage gate, plus at least 80% line coverage and 80% branch coverage separately for every Extensions and Scripts module and the startup snippet. Arguments skip the checker; after a selected run, use the full suite before invoking python3 tests/check_coverage.py coverage.json.

Tests exercise real App bundle discovery, boot, registry and menus with fake host owners and temporary preferences. Reporter behavior assertions are retained with imports redirected to bundle modules. Registration tests cover repeated enable, menu disable, unknown preferences and failed-save rollback. These offline checks do not establish native rendering, owner installation, installed artifact contents or publication. Keep the ordinary installed pre-push gate active.

docs.title: Remaining acceptance
docs.text:
Issue 210's source split is implemented: App's fontlabapp.plugins core owns scaffolding, discovery, registration and lifecycle; Plugmix supplies 50 manifest bundles under Extensions/ and one Show Reporters action. The deprecated fontlabapp.plugmix import shim and the separate fontlab_plugmix compatibility package remain distinct.

Qualify native Reporters palette/View > Reporters synchronization, toolbar and Tools > Tool, Window > Panels, startup, teardown, drawing and writer history on the exact installed tuple. Issue 211's nine native probes and four minor fixes remain separate. Issue 123 remains paused. Removing the compatibility package still requires a full consumer, distribution, source-recovery and licence audit.

docs.title: Website checks
docs.text:
Use a separate Python 3.13 environment and uv 0.13.7, installing the exact hash-locked src_docs/requirements.txt. Run sh src_docs/build.sh and python -m unittest discover -s tests_docs -v. These checks build complete catalogue pages without importing App or Plugmix. The build captures the source commit's timestamp once and both main-triggered jobs use it. A generated output child must be a direct docs-only child of the source SHA with identical non-doc source. The read-only second job checks the actual immutable output and requires full tracked and untracked parity.

Earlier recovery test results remain historical source qualification and do not qualify the current Extensions tuple. No product code, fixtures, startup script, recovery hash pin or licence is changed by this site. Publication, owner installation and native FontLab rendering remain separate. Private Pages configuration, permissions and requests stay owner-held.

docs.title: App Extensions
docs.text:
Install the reviewed fontlab-fontlabapp package in FontLab's Python 3.11 arm64 environment using App's install.vfpy. Install fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 and its providers before using this pack's bundles, action or optional startup snippet. The pack's install.vfpy requests Fly >=1.3.0 and App from its consumer dependency table. Manual copying requires preparing these dependencies separately; the legacy compatibility library keeps its App-only dependency. App's installer adds its marked startup block to initScript.py, preserving existing contents; the block calls App's core at launch. The optional initScript-snippet.py uses from fly.ap.plugins import install followed by install() to reach the same canonical App installer; it does not edit the startup file itself. The App core discovers the user-data folder from fontlab.flPreferences().dataPathDefault and scans its Extensions/ folder. Use FontLab's reported folder rather than assuming a platform path.

Copy the contents of this repository's Extensions/ into that folder, preserving reporters, filters, general, palettes and tools and their bundle folders. The pack contains 50 bundles: 39 reporters, five filters, four tools, one palette and one General plugin. Each bundle includes plugin.json and Python source; the bundles need no package install. Restart FontLab for startup discovery and after changing bundle source.

Open the Reporters palette from Window > Panels, or run the optional Scripts/Plugmix/Show Reporters.py action. Enable reporters in that palette or View > Reporters; disable them there too. Choices persist by stable ID, and saved choices are restored at startup. Without saved enabled reporter choices, reporters remain disabled. The source places tools in the toolbar and Tools > Tool, and palettes in Window > Panels. Native placement and synchronization still require verification on the exact installed tuple.

The Show Reporters action calls fly.ap.plugins.show_reporters(); it does not install packages or change the startup file. The retired per-reporter launchers and Install Plugmix Menu script are no longer used. Duplicate Anchor Rings retains set_handle_size(5|8|12), with a default of 8. Reporters do not edit font geometry. Startup, teardown, drawing and writer history remain native acceptance checks; these instructions do not claim those checks have passed.

docs.title: Coordinate-filter App requirement
docs.text:
The four coordinate filters require the coordinated App coordinate-writer change. Older App versions with the deletion-only Filter writer cannot apply them. No released App version has yet been assigned to this requirement; use the reviewed paired App/Plugmix source tuple, not the manifest minimum alone.

A partial native write follows App's existing PartialWriteError recovery: use Edit > Undo as directed by the error. It does not automatically roll back completed writes. Native Undo/Redo recovery remains unverified.

docs.title: Compatibility package
docs.text:
From an authorized checkout, install the compatibility package and its App dependency in the owner-managed FontLab Python 3.11 arm64 environment. In an isolated ordinary development environment, the package can be installed with uv pip install . once the required App distribution is available. Use native MeVisLab PythonQt inside FontLab, without another Qt binding.

Start the retained compatibility runtime explicitly with fontlab_plugmix.install() once per session. The optional initScript-snippet.py now targets App through fly.ap.plugins.install() and must not be combined with that legacy installer. No documentation build installs into FontLab's user folder.

docs.title: Runtime and preference ownership
docs.text:
Choose one runtime per session. Do not combine their startup installers or assume a preference migration guarantee. The shared filename is fontlab-plugmix.json in FontLab's Data directory. install(config_dir=...) selects an owned test directory. Runtime uninstall removes its owned actions, overlays and panels while retaining saved choices. Unknown preference keys survive; failed preference saves roll back activation. Preserve failed-teardown recovery rather than treating a partial teardown as success.

Filter, Tool and General choices default on until explicitly changed; palettes start hidden. Saved choices retain enabled, enabled_filters, enabled_palettes, enabled_tools, enabled_general and last-used params. The compatibility rename from nodes_outside_paths to offcurve_outside_bounds is an internal migration only.

docs.title: Licence and attribution
docs.text:
The repository retains Apache-2.0 terms and the Apache-2.0/MIT source-specific attribution in its NOTICE. The Extensions pack and compatibility package retain their own source history; the website does not add a new grant for upstream implementation bodies.

  • Download the exact repository LICENSE.
  • Download the exact repository NOTICE.

All product source and retained attribution remain unchanged. The MaterialX frontend also retains its bundled third-party licences and notices in generated assets. No Fly product licence has been copied here.

docs.title: Current English browser payload
docs.text:
The browser-component record binds the retained MaterialX 10.1.8 browser assets to exact upstream notices, package archives and source maps. Product terms above remain unchanged.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 35 unused lunr-languages 1.20.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. The build rejects theme/search-language, corpus, vendor-set/hash and local HTML-reference drift before removing them. Nine core vendor assets remain byte-identical. docs.title: Contour Picker
docs.text:
Bundle: Extensions/tools/ContourPicker.fontlabTool Stable ID: contour_picker

Select an entire local contour with one click. Activate Contour Picker from Tools > Tool or the toolbar, then left-click within 12 view pixels of any of its nodes. The contour containing the nearest node replaces the existing contour selection. Hold Shift to toggle that contour instead.

Both on-curve and off-curve nodes count, on open and closed contours. Equal distances prefer the first contour in snapshot order. Components are excluded: their decomposed contour indices do not identify editable local contours. Clicking with no nearby local node leaves the selection unchanged. The hit radius stays fixed as zoom changes; no usable scale means no hit.

Use it to select a small contour before applying Step and Repeat. This is a node-proximity picker, not a curve-distance or filled-area picker: a click near the middle of a long segment may miss even when it looks close to the outline. It changes selection only, with no geometry edit or geometry Undo step. There is no parameter dialog, drag selection or double-click containment behavior.

docs.title: Measurement Ruler
docs.text:
Bundle: Extensions/tools/MeasurementRuler.fontlabTool Stable ID: measurement_ruler

Measure an arbitrary span without selecting nodes. Activate Measurement Ruler from Tools > Tool or the toolbar, then drag with the left mouse button from one point to another. Release to retain the ruler; a new drag replaces it.

  • Hold Shift while dragging or releasing to constrain the endpoint to the nearest horizontal or vertical axis. Equal X/Y distances choose horizontal.
  • Press Escape to clear the ruler.
  • The label shows length in font units, signed dx and dy, and the angle counterclockwise from positive X, each to two decimal places.

Use it to compare a counter span or an offset visually. Endpoints follow the pointer: there is no node snapping, ink intersection measurement or guide creation. It works independently of components and curve types because it measures two points, not contours. Switching glyph/layer source or deactivating the tool clears the ruler. No geometry or selection is changed.

docs.title: Move Outlines
docs.text:
Bundle: Extensions/filters/MoveOutlines.fontlabFilter Stable ID: move_outlines

Translate drawn outlines while leaving spacing and attachment data in place. Open this filter from the Glyph menu, enter X offset and Y offset, and apply it to selected glyphs. For example, X = 10 and Y = 0 moves the outlines 10 font units right. Check anchors separately if they must follow the drawing.

Parameter Default Pure API allowed values X offset (dx) 0 font units Finite number Y offset (dy) 0 font units Finite number

Positive X moves right; positive Y moves up. Both zero leaves the outlines unchanged. This is an outline translation, not a sidebearing adjustment command.

App's numeric dialog fields use three decimal places. Fields without an explicit minimum or maximum use dialog bounds of −1,000,000 or 1,000,000 respectively; the pure parameter API accepts the values listed above.

docs.title: Scope and safety
docs.text:
The four coordinate filters require the coordinated App coordinate-writer change. Older App versions with the deletion-only Filter writer cannot apply them. No released App version has yet been assigned to this requirement; use the reviewed paired App/Plugmix source tuple, not the manifest minimum alone.

A partial native write follows App's existing PartialWriteError recovery: use Edit > Undo as directed by the error. It does not automatically roll back completed writes. Native Undo/Redo recovery remains unverified.

This filter changes every node of the selected glyphs' own outlines in the current master, including off-curve controls. It does not transform components, anchors or advance widths, and does not limit the edit to selected nodes. Node order, node flags, contour closure and native curve types are retained; curves are not flattened or reconstructed. App owns the guarded writer and geometry Undo step. Automatic layers and unsafe shared or transformed outlines are refused per glyph; safe glyphs can still be processed.

Empty outlines and unchanged results are no-ops. Non-finite parameters, non-finite coordinates and arithmetic overflow are rejected. Native dialog behavior, Undo/Redo and saved/reopened results remain unverified for the exact installed App/Plugmix tuple.

See installation and the Extensions catalogue.

docs.title: Node Probe
docs.text:
Bundle: Extensions/tools/NodeProbe.fontlabTool Stable ID: node_probe

Inspect node placement without changing selection. Activate Node Probe from Tools > Tool or the toolbar and hover within 12 view pixels of a node. The nearest node receives a ring and a label with its coordinates rounded to two decimals, its on-curve/off-curve status and its indexed provenance.

Local labels include contour and node indices (local 0:2, for example). Component labels also include the component index and base name. Indices start at zero. Component coordinates come from App's decomposed snapshot and are read-only; unavailable or skipped components cannot be inspected.

Use the label to distinguish a handle from an on-curve node, or to tell a local outline from a component. Both kinds of node participate in hit testing. At an equal distance, local nodes win over component nodes, then snapshot order wins. The 12-pixel radius stays fixed as zoom changes; no usable scale means no hit.

No modifiers or parameter dialog are provided. The tool does not select, move or reconstruct nodes, and it does not infer curve segments or distances to a curve. A glyph/layer source change clears the previous hover label.

docs.title: Round Outline to Grid
docs.text:
Bundle: Extensions/filters/RoundOutlineToGrid.fontlabFilter Stable ID: round_outline_to_grid

Round fractional outline coordinates to a regular grid before checking point alignment. Open this filter from the Glyph menu, set Grid spacing, and apply it to the selected glyphs. A grid of 1 rounds to whole font units; 0.5 gives half-unit positions. Review curves afterwards: rounding handles can alter their shape.

Parameter Default Pure API allowed values Grid spacing (grid) 1 font unit At least 0.000001

Coordinates are rounded independently to the nearest grid multiple. Halfway values round toward positive infinity: on a unit grid, 0.5 becomes 1 and −0.5 becomes 0. The grid is anchored at the glyph origin.

App's numeric dialog fields use three decimal places. Fields without an explicit minimum or maximum use dialog bounds of −1,000,000 or 1,000,000 respectively; the pure parameter API accepts the values listed above. The pure API accepts grid spacing down to 0.000001, but that precision cannot be entered in the current dialog. Use at least 0.001 in the dialog; a value rounded to zero fails validation.

docs.title: Scale Outlines
docs.text:
Bundle: Extensions/filters/ScaleOutlines.fontlabFilter Stable ID: scale_outlines

Resize drawn outlines about a fixed pivot. Open this filter from the Glyph menu, set horizontal and vertical percentages and the pivot, and apply it to selected glyphs. X = 90 and Y = 100 narrows outlines to 90% without changing height. With the default pivot, the glyph origin stays fixed.

Parameter Default Pure API allowed values X scale (%) (x_percent) 100% At least 0.001% Y scale (%) (y_percent) 100% At least 0.001% Pivot X (pivot_x) 0 font units Finite number Pivot Y (pivot_y) 0 font units Finite number

Each coordinate is scaled relative to the pivot. Negative and zero scales are not accepted, so this filter does not mirror or collapse outlines. Both scales at 100% leave them unchanged. Recheck spacing and anchor placement separately.

App's numeric dialog fields use three decimal places. Fields without an explicit minimum or maximum use dialog bounds of −1,000,000 or 1,000,000 respectively; the pure parameter API accepts the values listed above.

docs.title: Slant Outlines
docs.text:
Bundle: Extensions/filters/SlantOutlines.fontlabFilter Stable ID: slant_outlines

Apply a geometric shear to drawn outlines. Open this filter from the Glyph menu, set Rightward angle (degrees) and Pivot Y, then apply it to selected glyphs. An angle of 10° with Pivot Y = 0 leans points above the baseline to the right while keeping baseline points fixed. This is geometric slant, not optical correction.

Parameter Default Pure API allowed values Rightward angle (degrees) (angle) 0° −85° through 85° Pivot Y (pivot_y) 0 font units Finite number

The operation is x = x + tan(angle) * (y - pivot_y); Y stays unchanged. Positive angles move points above the pivot right and points below it left. Zero angle leaves the outlines unchanged. This does not change the font's italic-angle metadata. Recheck spacing, anchors and curve appearance separately.

App's numeric dialog fields use three decimal places. Fields without an explicit minimum or maximum use dialog bounds of −1,000,000 or 1,000,000 respectively; the pure parameter API accepts the values listed above.
